mainTopic: איסי בן יהודה's five undecidable פסוקים; the כהן גדול's path to the ארון with the קטורת, which בית המקדש the משנה describes, and how the קטורת was piled
overview: The amud finishes איסי בן יהודה's list of five פסוקים in the תורה that have no הכרע: שאת, משוקדים, מחר, ארור, and וקם. In each one, a word could belong to the phrase before it or to the phrase after it. A ברייתא shows that יוסף איש הוצל is the same person as איסי בן יהודה. The גמרא explains that his count of five covers only the תורה, since נביאים has more. It also explains that רב חסדא's doubt about a פסוק in שמות was a doubt only for רב חסדא, not for איסי. A new משנה describes the כהן גדול's path between the two curtains to the ארון on יום כיפור, the burning of the קטורת, and his short prayer. The גמרא asks which בית המקדש this could be. It proves that יאשיהו hid the ארון, and it answers that the משנה means the second בית המקדש and 'the place of the ארון.' Finally, אביי explains two conflicting ברייתות about where the קטורת is piled as a dispute between תנאים, and he begins a proof for one side that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First example: the word שאת
steps.stepSummary: The first undecidable word is שאת in the story of קין. It could mean forgiveness (your sin will be lifted away) or remembrance (your sin will be carried and remembered).
steps.simpleTranslation: [The first example is the word] 'שאת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the first of the five words that איסי בן יהודה said cannot be decided. It is the word שאת from ה׳'s words to קין in בראשית ד:ז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'הלוא אם תיטיב שאת ואם לא תיטיב.' If שאת goes with the words before it, it means 'If you do well, you will be forgiven.' If it goes with the words after it, it means 'You will carry your sin (it will be remembered) if you do not do well.' The words are the same, but the message changes from forgiveness to remembrance of sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting up; it can mean forgiveness (the sin is lifted away) or carrying the sin (it is remembered)
A deciding factor: a clear way to know how to read the פסוק
The תנא who made the list of five undecidable פסוקים
קין, the son of אדם, to whom this פסוק was said

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא writes only one word. It is not saying anything new about the word itself. It is pointing to a whole פסוק, and you have to read the words around שאת to see the problem.

phrases.english: 'Se'et' (lifted up).
phrases.notes: From בראשית ד:ז. It is unclear whether it means 'you will be forgiven' (read with the beginning) or 'your sin will be carried and remembered' (read with the end).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier statement of איסי בן יהודה (from the previous part of the daf) by naming its first example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word שאת in בראשית ד:ז is one of the five words in the תורה whose reading cannot be decided.

steps.title: Second example: the word משוקדים
steps.stepSummary: The second undecidable word is משוקדים in the description of the מנורה. It could describe the cups before it or the knobs and flowers after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The second example is the word] 'משוקדים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the second undecidable word, משוקדים, from the description of the מנורה in שמות כה:לד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'ובמנרה ארבעה גבעים משקדים כפתריה ופרחיה.' If משוקדים goes backward, the cups are shaped like almond blossoms. If it goes forward, the knobs and flowers are shaped like almond blossoms. This affects how the מנורה itself looked.

keyTerms.meaning: Made like almond blossoms
Cups, the decorations on the מנורה
Knobs, the round decorations on the מנורה
Flowers, the flower-shaped decorations on the מנורה

phrases.english: 'Meshukkadim' (made like almond blossoms).
phrases.notes: From שמות כה:לד. It could describe the cups before it or the knobs and flowers after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word משוקדים in שמות כה:לד can be read with either half of the פסוק, so its reading cannot be decided.

steps.title: Third example: the word מחר
steps.stepSummary: The third undecidable word is מחר in משה's instruction to יהושע about fighting עמלק. It is unclear whether the battle is tomorrow or whether only משה's standing on the hill is tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The third example is the word] 'מחר' (tomorrow).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the third undecidable word, מחר, from שמות יז:ט, where משה tells יהושע to fight עמלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'צא הלחם בעמלק מחר אנכי נצב על ראש הגבעה.' If מחר goes backward, יהושע should fight tomorrow. If it goes forward, יהושע should fight today, and only tomorrow will משה stand on the hill to pray. The timing of the battle depends on where the word belongs.

keyTerms.meaning: Tomorrow
עמלק, the nation that attacked ישראל in the desert
יהושע, משה's student, who led the battle
Hill, where משה stood to pray

phrases.english: 'Machar' (tomorrow).
phrases.notes: From שמות יז:ט. It could be 'fight tomorrow' or 'tomorrow I will stand on the hill.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word מחר in שמות יז:ט can be read with either half of the פסוק, so its reading cannot be decided.

steps.title: Fourth example: the word ארור
steps.stepSummary: The fourth undecidable word is ארור in יעקב's words about שמעון and לוי. It could curse their anger, or it could describe the 'cursed oxen' of שכם at the end of the previous פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The fourth example is the word] 'ארור' (cursed).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the fourth undecidable word, ארור, from יעקב's blessings in בראשית מט:ו-ז. This list will continue with the fifth word next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example is unusual because the choice is between two different פסוקים. One option reads 'ארור אפם כי עז': 'Cursed be their anger.' The other attaches ארור to the end of the previous פסוק: 'they cut down cursed oxen,' meaning the oxen of שכם, who came from the cursed כנען.

keyTerms.meaning: Cursed
שמעון and לוי, the two sons of יעקב who attacked שכם
שכם, the city (and its prince) attacked by שמעון and לוי
כנען, the son of חם, who was cursed by נח; שכם descended from him

steps.confusionAlert: Here the question is not only about which half of one פסוק the word belongs to. The word may belong to the end of the previous פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: All four words (שאת, משוקדים, מחר, ארור) share the same problem. A word sits between two phrases, and nothing in the text decides which one it belongs to. The fifth example, וקם, comes next.

phrases.english: 'Arur' (cursed).
phrases.notes: From בראשית מט:ז. It could be 'cursed be their anger' or the end of the previous פסוק, 'they cut down cursed oxen.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list; the list continues next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word ארור in בראשית מט:ז can be read with its own פסוק or with the previous one, so its reading cannot be decided.

steps.title: The fifth undecidable word: וקם
steps.stepSummary: The list ends with וקם in ה׳'s words to משה: it could attach to משה (you will rise) or to the people (the people will rise and stray).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the fifth word is 'וְקָם' (and he will rise / and they will rise).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the fifth and last word in איסי בן יהודה's list of Torah words that cannot be firmly read one way or the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'You are about to lie down with your fathers, וקם, this people will stray.' If וקם goes with the first half, משה will rise again, a hint to תחיית המתים. If it goes with the second half, it means 'this people will rise up and stray.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he will rise / and they will rise.' The fifth undecidable word
The rising of the dead, hinted at by one reading

steps.whatToRemember: The five undecidable Torah words are: שאת, משוקדים, מחר, ארור, וקם.

phrases.english: "And he will rise" (Devarim 31:16).
phrases.notes: Either 'you will lie with your fathers and rise' or 'this people will rise and go astray.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of five begun in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וקם is the fifth Torah word with no decisive reading.

steps.title: One sage with many names
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that יוסף איש הוצל and איסי בן יהודה are the same person, so his statements must agree. Yet a teaching in his name lists an extra undecidable verse beyond the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: יוסף of הוצל is the same as יוסף the Babylonian, who is the same as איסי son of יהודה, איסי son of גור אריה, איסי son of גמליאל, and איסי son of מהללאל. And what is his real name? איסי son of עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that many names belong to one sage. This sets up a problem: his two teachings seem to give different counts of undecidable verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יוסף איש הוצל and איסי בן יהודה were different people, two different counts would be no problem. Because they are one man, he seems to contradict himself: he says 'only five,' but elsewhere adds another verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?' Introduces a source that challenges
יוסף from הוצל, a town in בבל
A short form of the name יוסף

steps.confusionAlert: This list of names is not a side fact. It is the reason for the question. Since all these names are one person, his statements have to fit together.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Yosef of Hutzal is
phrases.notes: הוצל is a city in בבל.

phrases.english: the same as Yosef the Babylonian,
he is Isi ben Yehuda,
phrases.notes: איסי is a short form of יוסף.

phrases.english: he is Isi ben Gur Arye,
phrases.notes: גור אריה ('young lion') is a nickname for יהודה (בראשית מט:ט).

phrases.english: he is Isi ben Gamliel,
he is Isi ben Mahalalel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שְׁמוֹ — אִיסִי בֶּן עֲקִיבָא שְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: and what is his real name? Isi ben Akiva is his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of 'only five' by showing that the sage who adds another verse is the same person.
steps.kashyaTarget: איסי בן יהודה's statement that there are only five undecidable verses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same person, different counts, so he seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: Five in the Torah, more in נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The count of five refers only to the Torah. The extra verse comes from נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Torah there are no more. In the Prophets there are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by limiting the list of five to the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements are true because they speak about different books. 'Five' is the Torah's total. The added verse is from ספר מלכים, which belongs to נביאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the Torah (the חומש)
Of the Prophets
There isn't / there is

phrases.english: In the Torah there are none (beyond five),
in the Prophets there are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Five' seemed to be a total for all of תנ״ך.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Five' counts only the חומש. נביאים has more.

steps.title: רב חסדא's doubt about a Torah verse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא was unsure how to read a verse in שמות about the offerings at הר סיני. That seems to be a sixth undecidable Torah verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the Torah there are no more? But there is the question that רב חסדא asked: 'He sent the young men of בני ישראל, and they brought burnt-offerings of sheep, and slaughtered peace-offerings of bulls.' Or perhaps both kinds were bulls!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 7 by showing a Torah verse that רב חסדא also found undecidable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse, the word פרים (bulls) comes at the very end. רב חסדא asked whether it describes only the שלמים, with the עולות being sheep, or whether it describes both the עולות and the שלמים. That is the same kind of uncertainty as משוקדים, and it is in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Who asked (raised a question he could not settle)
Burnt-offerings
Peace-offerings
These and those, meaning both

phrases.english: And in the Torah there are none?
But there is what Rav Chisda asked:
"And he sent the young men of the children of Israel
phrases.notes: שמות כד:ה.

phrases.english: and they offered burnt-offerings of sheep,
phrases.notes: 'Sheep' is not in the verse. The גמרא adds it to spell out the first possible reading.

phrases.english: and slaughtered peace-offerings of bulls" —
or perhaps both these and those were bulls!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִדְאוֹרָיְיתָא לֵיכָּא וְהָא אִיכָּא דְּבָעֵי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 7's claim that the Torah has only five.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Torah has only five undecidable verses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא found another Torah verse unclear, which would make six.

steps.title: Doubtful to רב חסדא, obvious to איסי
steps.stepSummary: The verse was unclear to רב חסדא, but איסי בן יהודה knew how to read it, so it is not on his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב חסדא it was uncertain. For איסי בן יהודה it was obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sages simply see the verse differently. Only verses that איסי בן יהודה himself found undecidable are on his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'undecidable' depends on the reader's understanding. איסי בן יהודה had a clear reading of the שמות verse, so his count of five stands. רב חסדא's doubt does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: It was in doubt for him
It was obvious to him

steps.whatToRemember: איסי בן יהודה's five are Torah verses he himself found undecidable. נביאים has more, and other sages, like רב חסדא, may have doubts he did not share.

phrases.english: For Rav Chisda it was uncertain,
for Isi ben Yehuda it was obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַב חִסְדָּא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ לְאִיסִי בֶּן יְהוּדָה פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's doubt would make a sixth Torah verse for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt was רב חסדא's alone. To איסי the reading was clear.

steps.title: משנה: walking between the two curtains to the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The outer curtain was open on the south and the inner curtain on the north. The כהן גדול walked between them to the north, entered, turned south, and walked to his left along the curtain to the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The outer curtain was hooked open on the south side, and the inner one on the north side. He walks between them until he reaches the north. Once he reaches the north, he turns his face to the south and walks to his left along the curtain until he reaches the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the path the כהן גדול took on יום כיפור to bring the incense into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second בית המקדש there were two curtains with a gap of one אמה between them. Their openings were on opposite ends, so he could not walk straight in. He entered at the south, walked north in the corridor between them, entered the קודש הקדשים at the north, and then faced south. Facing south, his left side is east, where the curtain hangs. So he walked south with the curtain on his left until he was opposite the ארון.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The curtain separating the היכל from the קודש הקדשים
Hooked or clasped open at one end
Outer / inner
The Ark (or its place in the קודש הקדשים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Walks to his left' does not mean he turns and walks east. He has just turned to face south, so the curtain (on the east) is at his left side. He walks south along it until he is opposite the ארון.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַחִיצוֹנָה הָיְתָה פְּרוּפָה מִן הַדָּרוֹם,
phrases.english: MISHNA: The outer curtain was hooked open on the south,
and the inner one on the north.
He walks between them until he reaches the north.
Once he reaches the north, he turns his face to the south,
walks to his left along the curtain
phrases.notes: Facing south, his left side is east, where the curtain is. He walks south with the curtain on his left.

phrases.english: until he reaches the Ark,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַחִיצוֹנָה הָיְתָה פְּרוּפָה מִן הַדָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It returns to the יום כיפור service after the side discussion about undecidable verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול entered through the south opening, walked between the curtains to the north, then turned south and walked along the curtain (at his left) until he reached the ארון.

steps.title: Placing the incense and leaving with a short prayer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the כהן גדול placing the מחתה between the בדים, piling the קטורת, exiting the way he entered, and saying a short prayer in the outer chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reaches the ארון, he puts the pan between the two poles. He piles the incense on the coals, and the whole room fills with smoke. He walks out the same way he came in. He says a short prayer in the outer room. He does not make the prayer long, so that the people will not be frightened.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the route from step 10 and describes the actual burning of the קטורת inside the קודש הקדשים. It then describes how the כהן גדול leaves and prays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול now reaches the ארון and puts the קטורת on the coals until the room is full of smoke. He leaves 'the way he entered,' meaning he backs out while still facing the ארון. His prayer is kept short because a long delay would make the people outside fear that he had died inside.

keyTerms.meaning: The fire pan holding the coals
The carrying poles of the ארון
He piled up
The outer chamber, the היכל
To frighten or alarm

steps.confusionAlert: 'יצא ובא לו בדרך בית כניסתו' does not mean he turned around and walked out normally. He leaves along the same path, still facing the ארון, out of respect.

phrases.english: He reached the Ark —

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַבַּדִּים.
phrases.english: he places the coal pan between the two poles.

phrases.aramaic: צָבַר אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת עַל גַּבֵּי גֶּחָלִים,
phrases.english: He piled the incense on top of the coals,
and the entire chamber filled with smoke.
He exited and came out
by the same way he entered,
phrases.notes: He leaves facing the ארון, without turning his back.

phrases.english: and he prays a short prayer
in the outer chamber.
And he would not lengthen his prayer,
so as not to frighten the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the route from step 10, now reaching the ארון itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחתה is placed between the בדים and the קטורת is piled on the coals. The כהן גדול exits the way he entered and says only a short prayer in the היכל, so as not to alarm the people.

steps.title: Which Temple is the משנה describing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which Temple the משנה means. The first Temple had no curtains, and the second Temple had no ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Which situation are we talking about? If you say the first Temple, were there curtains then? If you say the second Temple, was there an ארון then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which בית המקדש the משנה is describing. It shows that neither choice seems to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions two curtains and also an ארון. The first Temple had a dividing wall (אמה טרקסין), not the two-curtain arrangement, so the curtain route does not fit it. The second Temple had the two curtains but no ארון, so placing the pan 'between the poles' seems impossible there.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing?
If you say
The First Temple
The Second Temple
Curtain

phrases.english: GEMARA
With what are we dealing?
If we say the First Temple,
were there curtains?
Rather, if the Second Temple,
was there an Ark?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה just learned by questioning which historical setting it could describe.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of curtains together with an ארון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two features of the משנה never existed at the same time. The first Temple had an ארון but not the two curtains. The second Temple had the two curtains but no ארון.

steps.title: Proof that the Ark was hidden away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves there was no ארון in the second Temple. When it was hidden, other holy objects were hidden with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: when the ארון was hidden, these were hidden with it: the jar of מן, the flask of anointing oil, אהרן's staff with its almonds and blossoms, and the chest the פלשתים sent as a gift to the God of Israel. As it says: 'Put the gold items you return to Him as a guilt offering in a chest at its side, and send it away, and it will go.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the claim from step 12 that the second Temple had no ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the ארון was hidden before the second Temple, so the question about the second Temple stands. It lists other objects that were kept next to the ארון and were hidden with it. The verse from שמואל shows that the פלשתים' chest was placed right beside the ארון, which is why it was hidden together with it.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא
Was hidden away
The jar of manna
The anointing oil
A chest or box
A gift

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
once the Ark was hidden —
the jar of manna was hidden with it,
and the flask of anointing oil,
and Aaron's staff
with its almonds and its blossoms,
and the chest that the Philistines sent
as a gift to the God of Israel,
as it is stated:
"And the gold items that you return to Him as a guilt offering,
put in the chest by its side,
and send it away, and it will go."
phrases.notes: שמואל א ו:ח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of step 12's question, that the second Temple had no ארון.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that there was no ארון in the second Temple.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the ארון was hidden along with the jar of מן, the anointing oil, אהרן's staff, and the פלשתים' chest, supported by a verse in שמואל.

steps.title: יאשיהו hid the ארון because of a coming exile
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that יאשיהו hid the ארון. He did so because of the verse warning that the people and their king would go into exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who hid it? יאשיהו hid it. What did he see that made him hide it? He saw that it is written: 'ה׳ will lead you and your king whom you set over you' into exile. So he arose and hid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds background. It tells who hid the ארון and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיהו read the verse in דברים that warns the king and the people will be exiled. He did not want the ארון to be carried off and shamed in exile, so he hid it. This explains why the ארון was missing from the second Temple.

keyTerms.meaning: יאשיהו, king of יהודה
He hid it away
What did he see? That is, what was his reason?
He arose and took action

steps.whatToRemember: The ארון was hidden by יאשיהו before the first Temple was destroyed. So the second Temple had curtains but no ארון. Steps 17-19 explain how the משנה can speak of curtains and the ארון together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This background shows that the question in step 12 is real. The answer must explain how the משנה fits the second Temple even without an ארון.

phrases.english: And who hid it —
Josiah hid it.
What did he see that made him hide it?
He saw that it is written:
"The Lord will lead you
and your king whom you will set over you,"
phrases.notes: דברים כח:לו, which speaks of exile.

phrases.english: so he arose and hid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 13, explaining who hid the ארון and why.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יאשיהו hid the ארון because he read in the verse that the people and their king would go into exile.

steps.title: The verse showing that יאשיהו hid the ארון
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from דברי הימים in which יאשיהו tells the לויים to put the ארון away so they will no longer carry it on their shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He said to the לויים who taught all of Israel and were holy to ה׳: Put the holy ארון in the house that שלמה son of דוד, king of Israel, built. You will no longer carry it on your shoulders. Now serve ה׳ your God and His people Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its claim that יאשיהו hid the ארון by quoting what he told the לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיהו tells the לויים to put the ארון 'in the house שלמה built.' This is understood as a hidden storage place that שלמה had prepared. 'You will no longer carry it on your shoulders' means the ארון would not be carried off into exile, because it would stay hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: King יאשיהו, who hid the ארון
The לויים who taught Israel
The holy Ark
A burden carried on the shoulder

phrases.english: As it is said: "And he said to the Levites
who taught all of Israel
who were holy to the Lord:
Put the holy Ark in the house

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה שְׁלֹמֹה בֶן דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built
phrases.notes: Understood as the hidden storage place שלמה had prepared

phrases.english: You will have no burden on the shoulder
phrases.notes: The ארון will not be carried away into exile

phrases.english: Now serve the Lord your God
and His people Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֹּאמֶר לַלְוִיִּם הַמְּבִינִים לְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that shows יאשיהו actually hid the ארון, as Step 14 stated

steps.title: How we know which objects were hidden with the ארון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר links the ארון to the jar of מן, the anointing oil, and אהרן's staff through three matching words: 'there,' 'generations,' and 'safekeeping.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: We learn it from the word 'there' that appears in both places, from 'generations' in both places, and from 'safekeeping' in both places.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the source for the ברייתא's claim (Step 13) that other holy objects were hidden together with the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words form a chain. 'There' links the ארון to the jar of מן. 'Generations' links the jar of מן to the anointing oil. 'Safekeeping' links the jar of מן to אהרן's staff. Because of these links, all these objects share the ארון's fate: they were hidden with it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from (a matching word)
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
'There' (links the ארון and the jar of מן)
'Generations' (links to the anointing oil)
'Safekeeping' (links to אהרן's staff)

steps.whatToRemember: The ארון, the jar of מן, the anointing oil, and אהרן's staff were all hidden together. So there was no ארון in the second בית המקדש.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
It is learned from "there" and "there"
phrases.notes: The ארון (שמות ל:ו) and the jar of מן (שמות טז:לג)

phrases.english: and it is learned from "generations" and "generations"
phrases.notes: The jar of מן and the anointing oil (שמות ל:לא)

phrases.english: and it is learned from "safekeeping" and "safekeeping"
phrases.notes: The jar of מן and אהרן's staff (במדבר יז:כה)

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָתְיָא שָׁמָּה שָׁמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual source for the list of objects hidden along with the ארון
steps.raayaObject: That the jar of מן, the anointing oil, and אהרן's staff were hidden with the ארון
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three גזרה שוה links between the ארון and the other objects

steps.title: The משנה means the place where the ארון used to stand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question from Step 12. The משנה is talking about the second בית המקדש, and 'reaching the ארון' means reaching the spot where the ארון used to be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה is talking about the second בית המקדש. What does 'he reached the ארון' mean? It means he reached the place of the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its question of which בית המקדש the משנה means. It answers: the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second בית המקדש had curtains, which fits the משנה, but it had no ארון. So the גמרא reads 'reached the ארון' as 'reached the place of the ארון.' This removes the problem raised in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the original assumption stands)
The second בית המקדש
The place where the ארון stood

phrases.english: Actually, it refers to the Second Temple,
and what does "he reached the Ark" mean?
The place of the Ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question in Step 12 after the ברייתא proved there was no ארון in the second בית המקדש
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The ארון' means the actual ארון, so no בית המקדש fits the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The ארון' means the place of the ארון in the second בית המקדש

steps.title: But the משנה mentions the ארון's carrying poles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the משנה says the מחתה was placed between the two בדים, which sounds like the ארון and its poles were really there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: 'He placed the מחתה between the two poles!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, using another phrase from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can explain 'reached the ארון' as 'reached its place.' But the משנה also mentions the בדים, the poles attached to the ארון. If there were no ארון, there were no poles. So how could he place the מחתה between them?

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (introduces a challenge from a source)
The pan holding the burning coals
The carrying poles of the ארון

phrases.english: But it teaches:
He placed the coal pan
between the two poles!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי: נָתַן אֶת הַמַּחְתָּה לְבֵין שְׁנֵי הַבַּדִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 17's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה speaks of the second בית המקדש, where there was no ארון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The poles belong to the ארון. If the משנה mentions the poles, it seems the ארון itself was present.

steps.title: Read it as 'as if between the poles'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה: he placed the מחתה 'as if' between the poles, meaning at the spot where the poles used to be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'as if between the two poles.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes one letter in the משנה's wording so that it fits the second בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of לבין ('between'), we read כבין ('as if between'). The כהן גדול put the מחתה at the spot where the poles had been when the ארון was there. Now every detail of the משנה fits the second בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way instead)
As if between

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה describes the second בית המקדש. 'The ארון' and 'between the poles' both mean the place where they used to be.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the ארון was back in the second בית המקדש. The כהן גדול only went to the empty spot where it once stood.

phrases.english: Say:
"As if between the two poles."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing a word in the משנה (לבין becomes כבין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Between the poles' means the poles were really there
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the spot where the poles used to be

steps.title: The משנה follows the view that he piles the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'he piled the קטורת on the coals' and comments that this follows the opinion that he piles it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He piled the קטורת on top of the coals.' The גמרא comments: our משנה follows the one who says he piles it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה and points out which opinion it matches. This also sets up the next question: if he piles it, where on the מחתה does he start?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'צבר' means to heap or pile, not to spread out. By saying 'תנן כמאן דאמר צוברה', the גמרא shows that there was another view, and our משנה follows the 'piling' side.

keyTerms.meaning: He piled or heaped up
The incense burned in the קודש הקדשים on יום כיפור
Burning coals
We learned in a משנה
In line with the one who says

phrases.english: He piled the incense
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: on top of the coals.
We learned it like the one who says: he piles it.
phrases.notes: As opposed to a view that he spreads it out

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of where the מחתה was placed to the next phrase in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows the opinion that the קטורת is piled on the coals.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about where he starts piling
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says he piles starting from the inner side, which is far from him. Another says he piles starting from the outer side, which is near him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: he piles it on the inner side, which is the far side from him. Another ברייתא teaches: he piles it on the outer side, which is the near side to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about which part of the מחתה he starts piling on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Inner' means the side toward the ארון, which is farther from the כהן גדול. 'Outer' means the side toward the entrance, which is closer to him. The two ברייתות give opposite instructions, so this needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: One ברייתא teaches
And another ברייתא teaches
The inner side, toward the ארון
The outer side, toward the entrance

steps.confusionAlert: Each phrase gives two descriptions of the same spot. 'פנימה שהיא חוצה לו' means one side: inner toward the ארון, but far from the כהן. It does not describe two places.

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
He piles it on the inner side, which is the far side from him.
And another baraita teaches:
He piles it on the outer side, which is the near side to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that we know he piles it, the גמרא asks where he starts, and finds two ברייתות that disagree
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about where the piling begins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two ברייתות give opposite instructions for the same act, so they appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the two ברייתות simply reflect two different תנאים who argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is an argument between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He says the two ברייתות are not meant to agree, because they come from תנאים who hold different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reading one ברייתא differently so that both fit together, אביי accepts that the disagreement is real. Each ברייתא reflects a different תנא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the leading teacher of his generation in בבל
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Abaye said: it is a dispute between Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the contradiction to a real dispute (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות should agree, so the contradiction is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות reflect two different תנאים, so there is no contradiction to explain away.

steps.title: אביי: The 'far side' view makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the more reasonable view is that he piles starting on the inner side, far from himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: it makes sense to follow the one who says he piles on the inner side, which is the far side from him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now picks which side of the argument is more logical. He is setting up a proof, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having said there is a real argument, אביי goes further and favors one side: starting the pile on the side near the ארון and far from the כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense

phrases.english: And Abaye said: it is reasonable
like the one who says: on the inner side,
which is the far side from him —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying the dispute, אביי chooses the more logical side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is more reasonable that he begins piling on the inner side, far from himself.

steps.title: אביי begins his proof from a משנה's warning
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to prove his view from a משנה that says the כהנים would teach the כהן גדול: 'Be careful.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: they teach him: 'Be careful...'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins quoting a משנה to support his view. The quote is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on what the כהן גדול is warned to be careful about. That warning, which comes next, will show that starting from the far side is the safer way.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
They teach him / instruct him
Be careful

phrases.english: As we learned: they teach him:
Be careful
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's claim in the previous step
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the piling starts on the inner side, far from the כהן גדול
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about the warning given to the כהן גדול when he burns the קטורת (continued on the next amud)
